thread:
Maria: Heads-up from the perf lab this AM — ran a cross-device autotune sweep (L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100). Focusing on kernel routing + seqlen-dependent paths. High-level: L4/T4 hit great throughput at short contexts but unstable tails once we cross ~512. A10 sits between but we see KV copy amplification on batch spikes. A100/H100 dominate long contexts.

Sam: Can you paste the distilled numbers so we can correlate to the CI alerts?

Maria: Trimmed numbers below (bs=4 except noted):
```
# device | seqlen | tok/s | p95
L4  | 64   | 3100 tok/s | p95=9ms
L4  | 512  | 900  tok/s | p95=110ms (kernel-path churn)
T4  | 256  | 1800 tok/s | p95=22ms
A10 | 1024 | 2700 tok/s | p95=40ms (kv memcpy @ bs>=8)
A100| 2048 | 5200 tok/s | p95=18ms
H100| 4096 | 9200 tok/s | p95=28ms
```

Jordan: That L4 behavior smells like selector oscillation after PR#4126 — we introduced a seqlen cutoff that can flip between int8_fused and fp16_tiled. If the scheduler probes both, we pay a kernel-switch tax.

Maria: Exactly. The autotuner currently treats each request as independent when deciding kernel route. Need a short-lived stickiness + warmup count so we don't flip on the first few probes.

Kevin: Proposal for selector logic:
- For device in {L4, T4}: use a stickiness window of 60s after route choice.
- Require N=40 warmup tokens (or 30 requests) observing steady latency before promoting an int8 route when seqlen in [192,512].
- Disallow int8_fused when bs >= 8 on L4/T4 (hard cap).
This should eliminate the p95 spikes and avoid int8 on heavy-batched cases.

Sasha: Also saw a KV cache path issue on A10: when batch_size rises we currently reallocate and memcpy whole prefix blocks. We can avoid ~15-25% extra memcpy by remapping offset pointers and only copying delta. I'll prototype a preserve-offsets-on-bs-change flag.

Maria: Good — add that to the runtime KV policy and we should instrument telemetry to tag when remap vs full copy happens.

Perf-bot: CI alert: PR 4126 increased L4 hourly p95 by +11% on baseline. See https://ci.redwood/4126/failure-trace

Sam: Ops is asking for a short-term conservative preset we can push to customers on low-memory tiers. Something that errs on safety (fp16 default, limited int8 ranges). Can we ship an opt-in preset?

Maria: Draft preset (example):
```json
{
  "preset_name": "conservative-lowmem-v1",
  "device_classes": ["L4","T4","A10"],
  "kernel_policy": {
    "default": "fp16_tiled",
    "seqlen_rules": [
      {"min": 0, "max": 128, "prefer": "int8_fused", "warmup": 20},
      {"min": 129, "max": 512, "prefer": "fp16_tiled", "warmup": 40}
    ],
    "hard_caps": {"int8_fused": {"max_bs": 7}}
  },
  "kv_policy": {"preserve_offsets_on_bs_change": "true"},
  "telemetry_tags": ["preset:conservative-lowmem-v1"]
}
```

Jordan: +1 to the preset. Add a metric sample tag for the selector decisions so we can query routes vs p95.

Kevin: Operational suggestion: add a runtime override flag for emergency rollback like `runtime.kernel.selector.override.{device_class}` that flips selector behavior without deploy. If perf-bot keeps tripping we can flip per-device quickly.

Sasha: That flag is trivial — will open a tiny PR to add the override hook and a guard in the selector.

Maria: Action items: 
- Sasha: PR for kernel.selector.override + KV offset remap (ETA: today)
- Jordan: Implement warmup + stickiness in autotuner, add selector telemetry (ETA: tomorrow)
- Maria: Add conservative preset, run 24h soak across dev cluster, collect telemetry (ETA: 48h)
- Ops: Prepare opt-in rollout plan and enable telemetry retention for 7d

Sam: Also want an automated e2e regression that ramps seqlen 64->4096 while varying bs to catch flapping. Put that under eng-runtime/e2e-tests.

Kevin: I'll add the test spec. Keep it lightweight (synthetic token generation) but deterministic so it runs in CI nightlies.

Maria: One more note: when we evaluate success criteria for the preset, let's track: p95 delta vs baseline (target <= +3%), token/s mean (target within -5%), and memory overhead. If any metric exceeds limits during the soak we revert.

Perf-bot: Regression window set to 24h for PR 4126; will re-evaluate after autotuner change lands.

Ops: If soak looks clean, we will make the preset available as opt-in and communicate to customers on low-memory tiers.

Maria: Thanks all — I'll post the soak results in ~48h and attach the telemetry query. :rocket:
